researcher_notes:
Covered the 7 remaining Labor/Workforce vendors (HotSchedules/Fourth already researched in the Back Office/Inventory batch, skipped per instructions). No usable rows existed in the 2026-07-21 candidate-evidence archive or archive_registry for any of these 7 vendors (checked by keyword across all 936 candidate rows and the 22 archive_registry entries -- zero hits), so this batch is entirely fresh web research.

Corporate-structure findings: (1) Sling was acquired by Toast, announced 2022-07-07 (Toast's second acquisition since its 2021 IPO), and now operates as 'Sling by Toast' -- flagged below. (2) Deputy remains independently owned and privately held (Sydney, Australia HQ; founders Ashik Ahmed/Steve Shelley), reportedly crossed a $1B+ valuation in 2024 per AFR/StartupDaily reporting; no IPO or acquisition found. (3) Legion Technologies remains independent -- raised $50M in debt financing from Silicon Valley Bank (announced 2024-12-12, on top of an earlier $50M Riverwood Capital equity round the same year), reported 216% revenue growth in 2025; no acquisition found. (4) 7shifts remains independent -- Series C closed 2024-12-01, $128M total raised, investors include Conexus Credit Union, SoftBank Investment Advisers, and Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality Group investment arm. (5) Push Operations (Vancouver, BC) remains independent, no acquisition found. (6) When I Work remains independent -- last raised a $200M private-equity round in Nov 2021, no subsequent acquisition found. (7) IMPORTANT NAME-COLLISION CAUGHT AND AVOIDED: a search for 'Homebase acquired 2025' initially returned strong-looking results about 'Homebase acquired by The Range / CDS Superstores, completed 2025.' This is a COMPLETELY UNRELATED COMPANY -- a UK DIY/home-improvement retail chain also named 'Homebase' that collapsed into administration in late 2024 and had its brand/stores bought out of administration by CDS Superstores (owner of The Range) in early 2025. The actual vendor in this category, joinhomebase.com (San Francisco, founded 2014 by CEO John Waldmann, SMB workforce-scheduling app), is unaffected -- it remains independent and privately held, last raised a $60M Series D on 2024-04-03 led by L Catterton Growth. Verified this distinction carefully before writing anything into the graph-adjacent notes below, per the standing instruction to verify rather than assume on corporate-structure questions.

Evidence-quality pattern across this category: three of the seven vendors (When I Work, Sling, Legion Technologies) came back with genuinely zero usable NAMED restaurant-brand evidence despite each vendor plainly serving restaurant customers. When I Work's own case-studies page features only single-location independents (a brewery, a food truck, a caterer, a board-game cafe) -- no multi-unit chains. Sling's customer-reviews page displays Subway and Taco Bell as bare customer-logo images with no case study, no date, and no location count behind them -- too thin to write a sourced record (a logo is not a dated claim). Legion Technologies genuinely publishes restaurant-sector case studies, but every one found is anonymized ('a leading fast-casual restaurant chain,' 'a popular restaurant chain') with the brand name deliberately withheld -- unusable given this schema requires a named brand. Homebase came back with only one small, low-confidence lead (Luxe Bites, 4 locations); its food-and-beverage customer roster otherwise skews toward single-location independent cafes/bakeries, consistent with its SMB-first market focus. By contrast, 7shifts, Push Operations, and Deputy all had substantive, dated, named-brand case-study libraries -- 7shifts in particular publishes 50+ dated restaurant case studies (though most are single-location independents; this batch selected only the entries with genuine multi-unit chain scale). One Push Operations lead (ZZA Hospitality Group, marketed on Push's own site as '700+ Location ZZA Hospitality') was checked against ZZA's own site and found to actually operate roughly 15 total locations across Boston Pizza (10), Crumbl (4), and Popeyes (1) franchises in Alberta/Saskatchewan/NWT/Yukon -- the '700+' figure could not be reconciled and was excluded as an unverifiable/likely-erroneous marketing claim rather than promoted on faith.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated 7shifts case study naming Pizza Ranch's Chief People & Strategy Officer (Ross Groeneweg) and a District Manager (Scott Parrill) by name and title, with a specific location count (150+ of 200+ total locations) and explicit framing as a head-office-endorsed preferred platform for franchisees.
records.notes: Pizza Ranch corporate designated 7shifts as its preferred scheduling/labor platform for franchisees; 150+ of the chain's 200+ locations were using it as of publish date. Not stated as literally all locations, so scored significant_deployed_footprint rather than brand_wide_deployment.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: When I Work -- zero usable named restaurant-CHAIN evidence found. The vendor's own customer-stories page features only single-location independent food & beverage businesses (BlackStack Brewing, The Donut Trap, Blue Plate Catering, The Castle board-game cafe) -- no multi-unit chains identified anywhere. No records added.

Sling -- zero usable DATED, sourced evidence found. Sling's customer-reviews page displays Subway and Taco Bell as bare logo images with no accompanying case study, location count, or date -- too thin to write a defensible sourced record per this batch's standard. No dedicated named-chain case studies found anywhere on getsling.com. No records added. (Also see corporate-structure flag: acquired by Toast in 2022.)

Legion Technologies -- zero usable NAMED restaurant-brand evidence found. Legion genuinely publishes restaurant-sector case studies (a 60+ location, 6,000+ employee fast-casual chain; a separate 'popular restaurant chain' case study), but both anonymize the brand name entirely -- unusable given this schema requires a named brand field. Legion's publicly named customers found elsewhere (Dollar General, Alo Yoga, Circle K, Cinemark, Bealls, Helzberg) are all non-restaurant retail/entertainment brands. No records added.

Homebase -- only 1 thin, low-confidence record found (Luxe Bites, 4 locations). Homebase's food & beverage customer base otherwise skews almost entirely toward single-location independent businesses, consistent with its SMB-first market focus; no multi-unit restaurant chain evidence found despite checking both its general customer-stories page and its dedicated food-and-beverage industry page.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: Sling -- acquired by Toast, announced 2022-07-07 (businesswire.com/PR Newswire coverage, corroborated by Restaurant Dive and Restaurant Business); now operates as 'Sling by Toast.' Not defunct -- the product persists and Toast actively markets it (getsling.com/toast/) -- but ownership changed and it is no longer an independent company.

Homebase -- NOT actually a corporate-structure change for the vendor in this category; flagged here only as a name-collision warning. A search initially surfaced a real 2025 acquisition of a company called 'Homebase' by CDS Superstores (owner of The Range), but that is an entirely unrelated UK DIY/home-improvement retail chain that collapsed into administration in late 2024. The actual Labor/Workforce vendor (joinhomebase.com, San Francisco SMB scheduling app) is unaffected and remains independent -- verified this distinction before writing any evidence into this file.
